identityReview: Graça Simbine Machel, born 17 October 1945 in Mozambique’s Gaza region, former education minister, humanitarian advocate, founder of FDC and the Graça Machel Trust, and co-founder/currently listed Deputy Chair of The Elders. Do not confuse her with Samora Machel or Josina Machel. Mozambique’s first education/culture minister is not prime minister; The Elders is not a UN office or religious body. UCT chancellor was a titular role from 1999 to 2019, not current executive university management. Lisbon language studies do not establish an earned doctorate; later honorary degrees remain distinct.
lifeStatusEvidence: The Nelson Mandela Foundation’s 9 November 2026 report explicitly states that she took part in the post-lecture panel at the Cape Town International Convention Centre on Friday 6 November. It records completed participation, not a planned appearance or inference from institutional activity under her name.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read relevant sections of The Elders, SAHO, Lisbon Academy, Morgan State and ACCORD biographies; the UN report cover/introduction/methodology in the INEE archive; the UCT farewell; the Trust’s November board announcement and home-page dating; and the Mandela Foundation event report. Read Commons metadata, licensing and upload history. Indexed-only results, inaccessible pages and unviewed recordings are separately identified.
corrections: Read The Elders’ biographical chronology and sections on education, the UN study, development work and organisational responsibilities. It identifies education-ministry service from 1975 to 1989, FDC founded in 1994, the UN expert appointment in 1994, the Nansen Medal in 1995, The Elders co-founded in 2007, the Trust founded in 2010 and appointment as Deputy Chair with Ban Ki-moon in October 2018. The current profile labels her Deputy Chair, not chair or a UN official. Its school-enrolment percentages describe different sex-specific endpoints and are not reproduced as a single uniform measure or a personal causal estimate. The 1999–2019 UCT role is historical. Broad evaluative praise and every other board role are not independently certified.

Read SAHO’s birth, Lisbon studies, FRELIMO and educational-career sections. It gives 17 October 1945 in Gaza, scholarship-supported language study in Lisbon, joining FRELIMO in 1973 and the 1974 Bagamoyo deputy-director appointment. It says her studies were interrupted; the dossier does not claim a completed bachelor’s or doctoral degree from Lisbon. This biography also has conflicting shorthand about resigning after her husband’s 1986 death versus service to 1989, conflicting educational percentages and stale current-office language; those passages are not adopted over institutional chronology. Its 11 November 1996 report reference does not replace the UN document’s explicit 26 August date. Precise marriage dates and claims about the plane crash were unnecessary and were not carried into the profile.

Read the Lisbon Academy’s biographical profile and membership metadata. It corroborates Mozambique/Gaza origins, study of languages in Lisbon, 1973 FRELIMO membership, initial appointment as education and culture minister and education service until 1989. It identifies later honorary doctorates as honours, not earned degrees from the earlier Lisbon studies. The 11 November 2008 election in the page header is academy membership, not her birth, graduation or ministerial appointment. The Nansen honour is dated 1995, while the British honorary damehood is a different 1997 distinction. Its approximate English title for the UN report is superseded by the document’s actual title. Other current positions were not comprehensively refreshed.

Read Morgan State’s historical commencement biography. It corroborates 17 October 1945, early teaching, the 1974 Bagamoyo deputy-director role, 1975 ministerial appointment, education service ending in 1989, FDC founded in 1994 and the 1995 Nansen Medal. The heading says she delivered a commencement address on 16 May 2015, but parts of the embedded biography are much older: it describes Mandela as living and a then-current crash inquiry. Those present-tense passages are not current evidence or a reliable date for underlying events. The page was used only for cross-checked stable facts, not current family status, positions, exact enrolment totals or a verdict on the 1986 crash.

Read the cover, introductory and methodology sections of UN document A/51/306 as preserved by INEE. The document is dated 26 August 1996 and explicitly identifies her independent-expert appointment as 8 June 1994 under General Assembly resolution 48/157. The Secretary-General transmits the expert’s report; it is not merely a unilateral UNICEF report, a treaty or an enacted domestic law. Methods included six regional consultations, field visits to several conflict settings and specialist contributions, covering recruitment, displacement, education, health and recovery. The study is not limited to Mozambique. The document date is distinct from later presentations or implementation. The entire 96-page report, its annexes and each underlying study were not independently audited.

Read the UCT council chair’s 13 December 2019 farewell letter. It confirms twenty years from 1999, the first woman and first Black person to hold this chancellorship, and the titular/representational nature of the office. Graduation ceremonies and high-level engagements are not the vice-chancellor’s daily executive administration. This farewell is evidence that the role ended in 2019, not that she remained chancellor in 2026; the precise last day is not inferred from the letter’s publication date. A video link was not watched. The author’s praise and incidental disaster/population claims were not adopted as independently verified facts.

Read ACCORD’s profile, including its distinction between civil-society governance positions and her former government role. It corroborates the Trust’s 2010 foundation and priorities in women’s economic/financial participation, nutrition, education and governance, as well as FDC and The Elders. These are organisational aims and activities, not proof that poverty, child marriage or gender inequality has been eliminated. The many board memberships and honours in this biography were not all separately refreshed. No hereditary or elected authority is inferred from courtesy titles; her founder role is not equivalent to the Trust’s chief executive.

Read the Trust’s 6 November 2026 board announcement and identify Shiphra Chisha as CEO from its explicit attribution. The quote is Chisha’s, not Machel’s; welcoming board members does not demonstrate Machel’s personal attendance at that event. The article names three appointees and distinguishes the founder’s vision from operational leadership. It does not state that Machel became a new CEO or that all programme goals were achieved. The home-page date supplies the year where the body says only 6 November. Other trustees’ achievements and legal-reform claims are not attributed to Machel or independently evaluated.

Read the Nelson Mandela Foundation’s 9 November 2026 report. It explicitly records the completed 6 November lecture in Cape Town and Machel’s subsequent panel participation with Santos, Yunus and a youth representative. Santos, not Machel, delivered the annual lecture, and his speech and Nobel award must not be attributed to her. This is the latest confirmed personal activity used here. The report also calls her earlier summit opening address Monday, whereas other sources describe 3 November, a Tuesday; the dossier uses only the unambiguous 6 November panel date. Publication in Johannesburg on 9 November is not the event’s location or date. No linked full video, speech or photograph gallery was reviewed.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No original educational credential, comprehensive ministry statistics, full UN report/annex audit, all current board memberships, underlying nonprofit impact evaluation, event video or portrait pixels were reviewed. Stable dates were cross-checked; conflicting school statistics, stale marital/current-office text and the summit opening-day discrepancy were excluded from definitive claims. Refresh current affiliations and recent activity before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and the English intermediary. Preserve language studies versus earned degree or honorary doctorate; FRELIMO teaching and deputy-director role; first education/culture minister versus prime minister; education service through 1989; 1994 FDC versus 2010 namesake Trust; founder versus CEO; 8 June 1994 expert appointment versus 26 August 1996 report issue; multi-region study rather than Mozambique-only research; Nansen Medal versus Nobel Prize; historical titular UCT chancellor versus executive university administration; nonprofit Elders deputy chair versus UN official; 6 November panel participation versus 9 November publication and Santos’s annual lecture.
